newsitem.title: UK: Gengold looks to double productivity.
newsitem.headline: Gengold looks to double productivity.

text.p: Gengold Ltd, South Africa's third largest gold miner, is looking to double productivity at its gold mines within three to five years, managing director Tom Dale told mining analysts on Tuesday.
"The target is to double our face advances and it should take us three years, possibly five years to realise that," he said.
Dale said the target was to get a sustainable level of productivity in the Gengold mines.

Currently the average face advance was 11 metres per worker, with a production blast roughly every three days. The target was to have a blast each day in the mines' 25 shift per month working programme.
He said to achieve that target across the six Gengold-run mines would require 800 new, qualified miners.
A training programme had already produced 150 newly qualified miners and another 80 would qualify in about six weeks. The programme was geared to produce 240 miners per year.
"Doubling productivity will not just start in three years. Productivity has started increasing already," he said.
However interim productivity increase targets were not feasible. "There are six mines all at different stages. It doesn't really work that way," he said.
He noted that at the Beatrix mine, face workers already had about 50 percent of their pay geared to productivity even after the nine percent wage rise agreed recently.
